description.narrative: (Thailand): The USAID Thailand Counter Trafficking in Persons (CTIP) activity follows the "4Ps" paradigm of Prevention, Protection, Prosecution, and Partnerships to reduce trafficking in persons (TIP) and better protect the rights of trafficked persons in Thailand. With FY 2024 funds, USAID Thailand CTIP will strengthen the capacity of the Royal Thai Government, civil society organizations, the private sector, media, academia, and at-risk communities and their collaboration to combat TIP. The activity will coordinate and complement other USG-supported CTIP programs in Thailand, including those funded by the U.S. State Department's Office to Monitor and Combat TIP, Bureau for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement, Federal Bureau of Investigation, and Homeland Security Investigations. Moreover, USAID will collaborate with other donors and international organizations to support the efforts of CTIP stakeholders in Thailand. To tackle emerging TIP patterns, such as trafficking of individuals into scam centers in countries neighboring Thailand to perpetrate cybercrime, USAID Thailand CTIP will foster cross-border collaboration to improve victim referral mechanisms and strengthen the capacity of government and non-government organizations to provide trauma-informed and rights-based support for trafficking victims and to raise public awareness about TIP linked to online scams. The activity will prioritize areas at increased TIP risks, including border areas, locations with high concentrations of migrant workers and vulnerable populations, government shelters, and priority industries (including fishing, construction, agriculture, and domestic work). This activity will increase Thailand's capacity and will to counter transnational crime relating to TIP, in alignment with the Thailand ICS and the U.S. Government's priority to end forced labor in global supply chains.
